messages:
eli: Quick find: /api/batch-classify examples show request body with fields in order { model, examples, top_k } but our OpenAPI example uses { examples, model, options } and the SDK snippets send `top_k` under `options.k`. This mismatch causes generated samples to look wrong.

sam: ugh, which file? link?

eli: docs/api/batch-classify.md section 'Request' + openapi/spec.yaml example. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3601

maya: thanks. The generator's example->snippet mapping assumes explicit param names; if examples schema doesn't match shape, snippet-tests fail. I can update the snippet generator to accept options.k as alias, but prefer fixing docs to canonical shape.

kevin: agree, canonical shape should be { model, examples: [ {input,label?} ], top_k }. Update OpenAPI example and snippets. Add a migration note for SDK users that used options.k.

docs-bot: deploy preview created: https://deploy-preview-3601--docs.redwood.ai (expires in 7 days)

sam: i'll take python/js snippets. eli can you update openapi/spec.yaml examples? I'll also add a small unit test in docs CI to validate example->snippet roundtrip.

eli: done; pushed OpenAPI example update to the PR. Also added a short compatibility callout showing mapping from options.k to top_k for older clients.

maya: pushed python/js snippet updates and test. CI shows one failing codegen test complaining about response example ordering: responses show `scores` before `predictions` which codegen asserts as the schema order.

kevin: ordering shouldn't matter semantically but tests are strict. change tests to schema-keyset equality rather than order, and for now make docs response show `predictions` first to match schema.

sam: updated tests to be keyset-equality in docs harness. will follow up with eng-platform to relax codegen assert.

eli: PR merged. created a short migration doc at docs/migration/batch-classify-shape.md and added a changelog line. Thanks all :thumbsup:
